title: AP Precalculus 2.8 — Inverse Functions
question: Inverse functions from a table and a formula, a restricted domain, a taxi fare backwards and a reflected point.
intro:
**Quick recap:**

- Reverse the pair:

\[
f(a)=b \iff f^{-1}(b)=a
\]

- To find \(f^{-1}\): write \(y=f(x)\), swap \(x\) and \(y\), solve for \(y\).
- The domain of \(f^{-1}\) is the range of \(f\).
- The graph of \(f^{-1}\) is the graph of \(f\) reflected over \(y=x\).
- \(f^{-1}(x)\) is not \(\dfrac{1}{f(x)}\).

**A calculator is allowed. Show your calculation before choosing A–D.**

questions.title: Table · Read the inverse
questions.prompt:
The function \(f\) is invertible.

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
x & 2 & 4 & 6 & 7 & 9\\
\hline
f(x) & 5 & 7 & 10 & 13 & 20
\end{array}
\]

Find \(f^{-1}(7)\).

questions.title: Formula · Find the inverse
questions.solution_title: Swap x and y, then solve for y

\]

euros.

questions.title: Graph · Point on the inverse
questions.prompt:
The point \((3,-1)\) is on the graph of an invertible function \(f\).

Which point must be on the graph of \(f^{-1}\)?
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(3) &= -1
\end{aligned}
\]

So

\[
\begin{aligned}
f^{-1}(-1) &= 3
\end{aligned}
\]

The point on \(f^{-1}\) is

\[
\boxed{(-1,\ 3)}
\]

- Swapping \(x\) and \(y\) reflects the point over the line \(y=x\).
- Not \((3,1)\): that reflects over the \(x\)-axis.
- Not \((1,-3)\): that changes both signs as well as swapping them.

takeaway: An inverse function runs the function backwards: it swaps inputs and outputs, so its graph is the reflection over y = x.
